claims.text: High-entropy alloys used for thermal insulation typically have complex, multi-element disordered structures.

A machine-learning model trained on high-throughput DFT/MD data containing disorder and phonon-scattering descriptors will predict phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys to within approximately ±10% of experimental values.
Configurational-disorder and phonon-scattering descriptors mediate the relationship between alloy composition and phonon thermal conductivity.
DFT/MD simulations can capture quantitative descriptors of configurational disorder and phonon scattering relevant to thermal transport.
Atomic disorder and phonon scattering interact to determine thermal transport in high-entropy alloys.
Including disorder and scattering information will allow the model to relate microstructural complexity to thermal transport more accurately than conventional simplified phonon-scattering models.
Current simplified phonon-scattering models or limited molecular-dynamics approaches do not fully incorporate configurational disorder.
Current simplified models typically deviate by more than ±20% from experimental phonon thermal-conductivity measurements.
The proposed model will reduce average prediction error from greater than ±20% to approximately ±10%.
The model will work reliably for high-entropy alloys whose compositional and microstructural features resemble those represented in its training data.
Prediction accuracy may decline for alloys with atypical or extreme microstructural disorder absent from the training data.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality and representativeness of the simulation data.
